title: Data Subject Erasure Across Data 360 Lake and Unified Profiles

steps.prompt: A customer submits a GDPR Right to Erasure request. Records exist in source CRM, Data 360 DLOs, unified DMOs, and derived insights. What must the architect ensure for complete compliance?

options.label: Execute a Data Subject Rights Forget Me request in Data 360 coordinated with source deletion to purge all layers
options.rationale: Data Subject Rights (DSR) requests in Data 360 ensure that personal data is deleted or masked across DLOs, unified profiles, and downstream search indexes, in alignment with source system erasures.

options.label: Delete the source Contact in CRM and rely on standard Data Cloud connector incremental syncs to cascade deletes
options.distractorAntipattern: Standard Data Cloud connectors append change records or soft deletes; they do not automatically purge historical lake data.
options.rationale: Standard data stream connectors append change events or mark deleted records, but do not physically erase historical immutable lake objects or derived insights.

options.label: Run an automated Data Transform to overwrite PII attributes with null values in harmonized Data Model Objects (DMOs)
options.distractorAntipattern: Overwriting fields in DMOs leaves raw PII stored in staging Data Lake Objects and immutable storage partitions.
options.rationale: Modifying DMO records does not remove historical PII residing in underlying Data Lake Objects, audit logs, or vector search embeddings.
